name: LegalOne
description: French *annonces légales* (legal notices) publishing — accountants and companies file required notices with competitive rates and compliance baked in. Bootstrapped, France.

mentions.evidence: ~$10.7k L30, ~$93k all-time, MRR listed as none / no active subscriptions (pay-per-notice model). Founded Oct 2025, France. Last sync Oct 1, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Digitize a mandatory local filing (legal notices, permits, company registry forms) and sell through accountants who already do the paperwork.

whyItPrints: Legal notices are mandatory, price-sensitive, and accountant-distributed. Transaction revenue (not seat MRR) with ~$11k L30 and ~917 users claimed — classic country compliance marketplace.
whyThisMatters:
French accountants use LegalOne to file the legal notices their clients owe. A new company, a registered-office move, a director change, or a closure all need one. You pick the formality and the département, prepare the text, and keep the papers with the firm. Shortcuts cover an SASU, an SAS, an SCI, a director change, an office move, and a dissolution. There are 42 forms. If the wording isn't ready, it can draft the notice in a few seconds. You see the price before anyone pays.

The client doesn't get a login. You send a payment link that lasts seven days. They pay. You keep the file, the invoice, and the status. A cashback credit from an eligible notice can pay for the next one. Search works by SIREN or by département.

It's bootstrapped, in France, started in October 2025. You pay per notice, so there isn't a monthly seat. The firm holds the file. The client just settles the link.

Law firms keep the matter files and the bills in one place.
